correctness.rationale: The normalized Beta moments yield the exact scalar kernel. Polynomial Cayley forms and exact Routh first columns for m=0..3 have strictly positive nonfinal entries for all t>0; their final entries change sign at unique explicit positive t values, with one simple boundary root at s=-1. For m=4, exact Routh first columns at t=1/2 and 4 have one and two sign changes, while t=1 gives (u+1)^5 and no scalar-disk zeros. The included checker independently reconstructs exact polynomial identities, verifies threshold algebra and 316 illustrative rational cases. No infinite claim depends on finite tests.

value.rationale: The natural structural question asks for the smallest nonnegative integer boundary-vanishing order at which varying origin mass can cause kernel zeros to return. The complete previously missing third-order threshold for every real t>0 distinguishes one-time zero loss from reentry; together with exact fourth-order witnesses it determines the first order m=4. This is a complete motivated integer cutoff in a standard two-parameter family, not just a selected numerical parameter slice.
